contributions.part: Mission lead: spacecraft, launch, mission control, sample return
contributions.role: Japan builds the spacecraft, launches it, runs the mission and handles the samples when they come back.

contributions.who: JAXA, Rikkyo University, Chiba Institute of Technology, Osaka University
contributions.role: Cameras (TENGOO, OROCHI — Rikkyo Univ.), laser altimeter (LIDAR — Chiba Tech), ion mass analyser (MSA — Osaka Univ.) and the coring sampler (C-SMP — JAXA).

contributions.part: CMDM, IREM, SHV, Sample Return Capsule
contributions.role: Dust monitor (CMDM — Chiba Tech), radiation monitor (IREM), high-definition camera (SHV) and the capsule that carries the samples to Earth (SRC).

contributions.who: NASA · built by Johns Hopkins APL
contributions.role: Reads which chemical elements are on Phobos's surface from the gamma rays and neutrons coming off it.
Blows high-pressure nitrogen gas to lift surface grains into a container. It takes only the top layer, and backs up the coring sampler.
contributions.note: DLR's facts page lists P-SMP among the exploration-module instruments under “JAXA”. JAXA, CNES and ISAS say NASA provided it.

contributions.role: Helps track MMX, send commands and receive mission data, alongside JAXA's own stations.

contributions.who: CNES · LIRA (Observatoire de Paris-PSL) · 9 French labs
contributions.role: Finds out which minerals are on Phobos and Deimos from the light they reflect, and looks for water and organic matter. CNES built its ground segment and will operate it.
Helped design and check MMX's orbits around Phobos, including low ones; works on navigation and on Phobos's orbit and gravity field.

Scout, demonstrator and explorer: checks the ground before MMX lands, tests driving where gravity is nearly 2,000 times weaker than on Earth, and looks at the soil in detail down to 0.1 mm. Planned: 100 days, up to 100 m.

contributions.part: Rover cameras, computer, power and radio
contributions.role: Two navigation cameras, two wheel cameras and the central service module are French. OCA coordinates the rover science on the French side; ISAE-SUPAERO and LAM work on the camera science.

contributions.part: miniRAD — infrared radiometer on the rover
contributions.role: An infrared radiometer. It comes from MARA, an instrument on MASCOT — the small lander that rode on Hayabusa2.

contributions.who: DLR · INTA & University of Valladolid · Univ. of Tokyo, JAXA & Rikkyo Univ.
contributions.part: RAX — Raman spectrometer on the rover (1.5 kg)
contributions.role: One instrument, three countries: Germany built the spectrometer, Spain the laser (a flight spare of the ExoMars laser), Japan the autofocus. It identifies minerals on Phobos's surface.
The rover will be driven from Toulouse and Cologne, with the two teams taking turns.
A drop tower and microgravity simulation for testing.
Radio equipment for talking to Earth. In return, two ESA scientists sit on the MMX science board.
Helps track MMX, send commands and receive mission data, alongside JAXA's own stations.
In 2031 the sample capsule is planned to land in the Woomera Prohibited Area in South Australia.
